feature: Text that grows in a video moves as one piece
summary: Words that zoom or scale in a video now move as one solid piece, with no letter jumping on its own, as it plays and in the exported file. Zooms on a recording, shapes, pictures and camera pushes hold just as steady.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed. The same thing as a script is the walk words-that-grow-move-as-one-walk.

try.do: Watch the before and after reel, full size above and 4x below, twice at speed and once at quarter speed.
Look at one letter before and after across the zoom.
File > New > Video, press T, click the canvas and type a few words.
In Properties press Add Key's arrow > Animate a Property > Scale, type 50, step on one second and type 100.
Press Space and watch the letters as the title grows.
Change the first key to 98 and play again: a slow drift, where jitter shows most.
Open a recording, add a zoom on it and play: the words in the recording glide instead of stepping.

evaluate: Do the letters of a growing title hold together, with nothing jumping on its own?
Is a still title as sharp and as heavy as it was before?
Is the zoom on your own recording smooth now?
Does the video that started this look right when you export it again?
rough: Cause, measured: each letter was redrawn by the system on every frame, snapped to its own part of a pixel (0.58 px apart on its own), and the words were set again at every in-between size, which spaces them a little differently each time (0.97 px with both). The picture was also rounded to whole pixels and stretched back, and Core Image rounds the box of a scaled layer, a quarter to a third of a pixel on shapes and pictures. A zoom on a recording cut its window on whole pixels: 1.5 px at worst.

Numbers, worst letter against the word, before to after: the walk's title 0.50 to 0.007 px as it plays and 0.63 to 0.007 px in the export; 1080p and 4K type 0.40 to 0.69 before and 0.005 to 0.04 after; a 2 percent drift 0.69 to 0.009; the built-in titles that grow 0.59 to 0.70 before (Keynote Section, Gradient Word, Spotlight) and under 0.01 after; text in a group 0.03; camera push 0.08 to 0.006; box and oval 0.3 to under 0.001; picture 0.23 to 0.03; zoom on a recording 1.3 to 1.5 before and 0.01 to 0.03 after. Slow turns were already steady.

Ruled out: no cache switched between two sizes, and no stepped zoom. Found on the way: type 59.9999 points tall is spaced by the system as 59, so a title could step by 0.05 percent on some frames; fixed.

Sharpness of a title that never grows, against the same words on a still picture (which the system draws): 0.99 to 1.06 times at 14 to 120 points, weight within 1 percent. A title that is keyed to grow rests 1 to 2 percent softer, because its letters may not snap to whole pixels without slipping again. A zoomed recording is sharper than before: 118 against 108 at 1.3x, 76 against 61 at 2x.

Frame cost, release build, 8 titles: scaling at 1080p 6.9 to 5.9 ms, at 4K 14.0 to 12.3 (worst 25 to 14), letters coming in while scaling 22.7 to 21.0, sliding unchanged. A camera pushing in on 8 titles went from 2.6 to 5.4 ms: the words are now drawn at the size they are seen, so they stay sharp.
Labels on arrows still slip 0.48 px when they are scaled in a video; filed as labels-on-arrows-and-measurements-move-as-one-sm.
The video that prompted this was not available, so it is checked on titles, zooms and camera moves made the same ways rather than on that file.
